ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based client due diligence under FIC Act 38 of 2001; screen all UBOs, directors, authorized representatives and counterparties against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated List, South African FIC and National Treasury sanctions lists, and domestic terrorism financing lists; mandatory enhanced due diligence where a beneficial owner is a domestic or prominent foreign PEP or a family member/close associate of a PEP, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification; ongoing transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting under section 28A of the FIC Act; record retention for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal (eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate suffixes must appear in the precise form 'Proprietary Limited', 'Pty Ltd' or 'Pty Limited'; names may be submitted in any official South African language but must be transliterated into Latin-script characters for CIPC indexing; the name must not be offensive, misleading, falsely imply state affiliation, or be unduly similar to an existing registered name or trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name may be extended by filing a renewal application through CIPC e-Services before expiry; if the name is rejected, administrative reconsideration may be filed within 10 business days, accompanied by supporting evidence; if CIPC upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of Companies Act 71 of 2008, and thereafter to the High Court on procedural or legal grounds; alternative acceptable names should be included in the original filing to avoid loss of reservation time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual registered office is permissible only if a physical South African street address is designated for service of legal process and CIPC correspondence, and if the provider maintains actual mail-handling and inspection access; a post-office box or private bag alone is insufficient. For this fertilizer wholesale trading business, banks and FIC-supervised institutions will generally accept a compliant virtual office, but SARS may challenge the location of effective management and require physical records-preview facilities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium risk: approximately 40% unannounced inspection probability within the first 24 months, driven mainly by FIC risk-based AML/CFT supervision and SARS compliance verification; CIPC itself does not routinely inspect, but the registered office must permit authorized inspection of statutory records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 13, 14, 19, 50 and 66, read with the Companies Regulations, 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, Pretoria, South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A), filed electronically via CIPC e-Services
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The Companies Act 71 of 2008 allows zero or nominal par-value shares and no escrow account requirement; any subscription consideration must be paid into the company's bank account and recorded in the company's register as issued capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, as certified by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, is ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER that the allotment and issue of 100 ordinary no-par-value shares to the founding subscriber, for a board-determined consideration paid into the company bank account, are approved. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office specified in the Notice of Incorporation is adopted as the company's legal seat and address for service. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors and officers named in the incorporation schedule are appointed effective from the date of incorporation, and that the chairperson and managing director are authorised to execute ancillary filings and registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of company name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal - Name Reservation module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into CIPC e-Services, complete Form CoR 9.1 (Notice of Reservation of Name), pay the name reservation fee and submit the proposed company name for pre-approval. The name must satisfy the restrictions in section 11 of the Companies Act, including absence of undesirability, offensiveness and conflict with existing trademarks.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 9.1
Certified identity document or passport of founding shareholder/director
Power of attorney for a registered agent (if applicable)
Proof of any required trademark-holder consent (if the name contains protected elements)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, file a new name reservation through CIPC e-Services or, within the statutory objection period, file a complaint with the Companies Tribunal; any unresolved CIPC non-compliance may be remedied by applying to the High Court for a mandamus.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal - Company Incorporation module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) and attach the company's Memorandum of Incorporation on Form CoR 15.1A. Submit the registration package electronically through CIPC e-Services, pay the prescribed filing fee, and retain the CIPC transaction reference number.
required_dossiers: Executed Form CoR 14.1
Executed Form CoR 15.1A containing registered office, directors and share class
Certified identity documents of initial directors
Consent letters from each director
CIPC name reservation certificate or reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the filing, cure the stated deficiency in e-Services and resubmit without a new fee; if CIPC rejects the application, use the internal reconsideration process and, where necessary, approach the Companies Tribunal or High Court for relief.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of incorporation certificate and company data verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the approved filing in CIPC e-Services and download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the company name, registration number (YYYY/XXXXXX/07), address, directors and share capital details; correct any discrepancies promptly.
required_dossiers: CIPC electronic Certificate of Incorporation
Approved Memorandum of Incorporation
CIPC company information report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed or contains errors, submit a correction request to CIPC through e-Services, supported by an affidavit and the original approved MOI, and escalate to the CIPC Customer Contact Centre if no response is received within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the South African Revenue Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - branches and eFiling
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax and VAT (if taxable annual supplies exceed or are expected to exceed the compulsory VAT threshold of ZAR 1 million, or if voluntary registration is elected), and for PAYE if employees will be engaged. Use SARS eFiling or visit a SARS office with the required dossiers.
required_dossiers: CIPC registration certificate and approved MOI
Bank confirmation of the company's bank account
Directors'/members' personal details and physical business address
SARS VAT/income tax registration declarations
Power of attorney or tax representative resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS issues a query or rejects the registration, respond in writing through eFiling, request a SARS tax clearance or escalation to the SARS branch manager, and invoke the dispute/objection procedure under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with UIF and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour - Unemployment Insurance Fund and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and the Compensation Fund for occupational injuries and diseases. Submit the employer declaration and obtain the UIF reference number and COIDA clearance certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and MOI
Physical business address proof
Identity documents of directors and employees
Company banking details
Completed UIF registration form and COIDA declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is objected to or delayed, provide the requested corrective information before the deadline, escalate to the Department of Employment and Labour regional office, and if necessary appeal to the Director-General under the labour legislation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of business bank account and deposit of share consideration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorised under the Banks Act 94 of 1990; SARB Authorised Dealer for exchange-control matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a business current account in the company's name, submit FIC-compliant beneficial-ownership documentation, and deposit the agreed initial share consideration into the account. Obtain a bank confirmation letter for SARS and future financing use.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and approved MOI
SARS registration certificates
Resolution of the board appointing bank signatories
Beneficial ownership declaration/register
Proof of physical business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests supplemental FICA information, deliver the completed beneficial-ownership schedule and sources of funds within the bank's stated deadline; if the account is still declined, appoint new signatories or approach another authorised bank and file an internal complaint with the bank's compliance officer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Registrar of Fertilizers, Farm Feeds, Agricultural Remedies and Stock Remedies, Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development (DALRRD)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Fertilizer Product Registration Certificate and Fertilizer Importer/Wholesaler Registration under the Fertilizers, Farm Feeds, Agricultural Remedies and Stock Remedies Act 36 of 1947

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and the provincial environmental department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment or full Scoping/EIA under the 2014 Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations depending on dangerous-goods storage thresholds; facilities below the listed threshold require a compliance/registration notice, and wholly exempt storage operations require an environmental management site plan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No discharge of wastewater or trade effluent without a Section 21 water-use licence under the National Water Act, 1998; air emissions must meet the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act, 2004 national ambient standards and any atmospheric emission licence requirements; bulk urea dust and ammonia fugitive emissions controlled; waste handling must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and emergency plan approved by the local fire authority; structural load inspection certificate for warehouses, racking and flooring; Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 compliance and risk assessment; municipal dangerous-goods storage approval and Disaster Management Act 57 of 2002 integration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); SARS eFiling portal (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za) and principal website (https://www.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African-incorporated Proprietary Limited Company is automatically registered for income tax through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) integration at incorporation, obtaining a SARS income tax reference number. For VAT, compulsory registration must be applied for within 21 days of the taxable supplies exceeding R1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration is available from R50,000 using Form VAT 101. Foreign (non-resident) entities carrying on a South African enterprise must register with SARS via eFiling as a non-resident company and may appoint a representative taxpayer; a single taxpayer reference number (TIN) covers income tax, VAT, PAYE, and customs duties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists. Available elections under the Income Tax Act and VAT Act include: (i) Section 45 election for tax-neutral intra-group asset transfers; (ii) Section 47 election for intra-group share transfers; (iii) Section 24J election for compound interest instrument recognition; (iv) Section 11D election for R&D allowance certification; (v) Section 50 VAT Act group of companies registration election; (vi) deemed vendor payment-basis VAT accounting election under Section 15(2A); (vii) hybrid debt-equity instruments are subject to mandatory Section 8F/8FA treatment with limited anti-mismatch elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) — Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory threshold: R1,000,000 (taxable supplies exceeding R1 million in any 12-month period); voluntary registration permitted from R50,000; foreign electronic-services suppliers must register when annual supplies exceed R1,000,000
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. VAT invoices must satisfy Section 20 of the VAT Act (15 prescribed fields). Electronic tax invoices are permitted. SARS requires submission of VAT returns and transactional data via eFiling and the VALID (VAT Automated Ledger Interface) API for large vendors; customs export declarations are filed electronically through the SARS Customs EDI using the SAD500. Continuous digital data extraction powers under Section 40 of the Tax Administration Act enable SARS to match e-invoicing, customs, banking, and foreign-exchange data without a live clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, a supply of fertiliser goods (prilled urea and potassium chloride) is zero-rated only if the goods are supplied under a sale to a non-resident (export consignee) and are removed from South Africa within 90 days of supply (or within a longer period approved by SARS, including up to 5 years for goods stored under permit). Section 11(2)(l) zero-rates services supplied to non-resident persons where the services are physically rendered outside South Africa. For wholesale exporters, the vendor must hold documentary proof of the export transaction, including proof of payment in foreign currency received through an authorised dealer bank.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) duly cleared by SARS Customs
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of goods from South African territory
Commercial Invoice referencing supplier and recipient VAT registration numbers
Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/telegraphic transfer advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds within 180 days
Export permit or SARS letter for conditional exports (where applicable)
Proof of supply and contract documentation identifying the non-resident customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disallow zero-rating retrospectively where export documentation is insufficient or goods are not removed within the statutory time frame, resulting in a deemed taxable supply at 15% with interest calculated from the original date of supply. Under Sections 222-223 of the Tax Administration Act, understatement penalties range from 10% (standard case) to 25% (substantial non-disclosure), 75% (gross negligence), and 100% (intentional tax evasion); an additional 10% SARS penalty may apply for failure to pay. Criminal prosecution for fraud, customs contraventions, or aiding non-compliance can result in fines and imprisonment. Vendors claiming export zero-rating must retain all supporting evidence for a minimum of 5 years from the date of supply, and SARS cross-matches export declarations with bank exchange-control records to detect fictitious exports.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as the delegated Exchange Control Authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act No. 9 of 1933), the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, and the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers. All foreign exchange transactions in South Africa must be routed through an authorised dealer in foreign exchange, being a commercial bank licensed by SARB and the Prudential Authority of the Financial Sector Conduct Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods, services, dividends, and interest, subject to reporting requirements and documentary verification by an authorised dealer. Capital account transactions, such as non-resident equity injections and shareholder loans, require completion of inward foreign investment forms and valid commercial rationale; repatriation of capital and profits is permitted for registered non-resident investors, but is subject to verification via the company registry, the non-resident share endorsement, evidence of the original inward transfer, and compliance with SARS tax clearance or exemption requirements. No blanket convertibility restriction applies, but non-trade outward remittances above prescribed thresholds require FinSurv approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Every exporter of urea and potash must, within 180 days of date of shipment, repatriate the full export sales proceeds to South Africa via an authorised dealer. The proceeds must be received in the prescribed invoice currency and either sold to the authorised dealer against ZAR or credited to a resident Foreign Currency Account (FCA) maintained with the authorised dealer. There is no mandatory percentage conversion of export earnings into ZAR under the current exchange control framework, but the full gross proceeds must be reported and matched to the relevant SAD500 customs export declaration and supporting shipping documents; any deviation or unrepatriated balance requires a completed application for expatriation of export proceeds and may attract SARB penalty action.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not licensed as authorised dealers in foreign exchange and are not permitted to hold ZAR client deposits or execute exchange control transactions under the Banks Act, 1990 and the National Payment System Act, 1998. They may be used only as ancillary front-end interfaces to a licensed South African bank where the ultimate clearing and custody remain with that bank. For capital escrow, trade settlement, and FX compliance, a direct relationship with a Tier 1 South African commercial bank is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (FICA), the bank must identify and verify all natural person beneficial owners and authorised signatories before opening a corporate account. In practice, for a non-resident owned (Pty) Ltd, the bank will require at least one director or a designated executive appearing physically at an in-person KYC interview at the branch, especially for a capital escrow account. Remote onboarding is available only where the bankâ€™s internal policy permits digital FICA verification using live biometric checks and electronic verification of identity documents; however, the on-boarding timeframe is materially extended without physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholding being routed through a trust, private foundation, or holding company with an opaque beneficial ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate registry excerpts from all jurisdictions in the chain; CIPC Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation; CFO (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) Beneficial Ownership Register; notarised shareholder register; board resolution approving share issue; sworn affidavits confirming the economic substance of each holding company; references from relationship banks in the source jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags on bulk urea/potash import settlements, including over-invoicing, under-invoicing, or double-issuing invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase contract; pro-forma invoice; independent commodity benchmark price evidence (e.g., CRU or IFA fertiliser indices); bill of lading; packing list; weight and quality inspection certificates from SGS, Bureau Veritas, or Intertek; marine insurance policy; South African Customs import declaration SAD500; supplier bank account confirmation and original correspondence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure triggered by purchase from Russian, Belarusian, or Iranian potash or urea suppliers on the OFAC/EU/UN sanctions list or with blocked shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed sanctions screening results for the supplier, beneficial owners, and shipping vessels; international trade compliance opinion letter; origin certificates confirming product origin and no re-export prohibition; UN and EU general licence review; bank compliance approval; end-user undertaking; full chain of title documentation and freight manifest with underlying maritime risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment arrangements, where the fertiliser seller instructs payment to an unrelated intermediary or a factoring financier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written and duly notarised letter of assignment from the supplier; assignment agreement; original invoice with notation of the assigned payment route; due diligence report on the third-party payee; signed acknowledgment from the supplier that payment is for its account; board resolution and sworn explanation of the commercial reason for third-party settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually slow repatriation of export proceeds, which for an export-trading entity may indicate circulation of funds outside the exchange control net.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export contract; vessel manifest; Port of loading terminal cargo documentation; SAD500 export declaration; freight and inspection invoices; bank credit advice; aged trial balance of export debtors; explanatory affidavit from the CFO; application to the authorised dealer for late-receipt approval where the 180-day limit has been exceeded.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All non-resident equity and shareholder-loan capital injections for fractional or full ownership of the South African (Pty) Ltd must be routed via the authorised dealer bank using a standard SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the non-resident investorâ€™s foreign bank, with remittance instructions clearly stating the purpose as non-resident direct investment capital injection in the South African corporate. The authorised dealer will require the prescribed inward foreign investment approval form (Form FI) for equity and the loan approval form for shareholder loans, together with the companyâ€™s updated CIPC registration record, board resolution, bank account opening specimen mandates, and beneficial ownership declarations. The bank will report the transaction to SARB FinSurv under the correct Balance of Payments purpose code for direct investment equity and loan liabilities; the transfer must be credited to the ZAR or designated foreign currency account of the entity and may not flow through an offshore EMI, crypto exchange, or third-party intermediary. For any loan injection, a conformed loan agreement and an internal approval from the SARB Authorised Dealer are required to secure applications for future outgoing loan repayments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for the import of urea and potash should be effected by commercial documentary Letters of Credit issued by the South African bank in favour of the overseas supplier, using SWIFT MT700, or by direct SWIFT MT103 wire transfers where the commercial relationship supports open account terms. The authorised dealer must hold or verify the following documentation before settlement: the underlying import purchase contract and pro-forma invoice, an invoice not exceeding benchmark value, transport documents (bill of lading, sea waybill, or CMR), customs SAD500 declaration, and evidence that the BOP purpose code designated for agricultural commodity imports is correctly stated. For open-account imports, the bank will apply a creditor payment scrutiny process, and the importer must file a Form AID or creditor payment indication in accordance with the Currency and Exchanges Manual. Letters of credit provide the strongest clearing rail for trade settlement, permitting the bank to control presentation of documents against payment; direct MT103 settlements are acceptable only when the supplier, the entity, and the market relation meet the bank's enhanced due diligence requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) with an authorised dealer, recognised as a deliverable ZAR/USD forward, for hedging firm or anticipated import and export exposures on urea and potash trade settlements

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) executed solely through a licensed authorised dealer where the underlying exposure is arbitraged offshore or where the transaction qualifies for NDF treatment under SARB FinSurv guidelines

Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) for medium-term shareholder loans or international trade financing, approved by the authorised dealer and recorded with SARB where the loan value exceeds prescribed threshold
Deliverable currency swap between ZAR and USD or EUR for temporary working-capital mismatches in commodity trade settlement

Currency options (call/put) purchased from a South African authorised dealer for hedging the USD/ZAR purchase or sale requirement, subject to the maturity and size being commensurate with the entity's gross trade flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing administrative penalty of ZAR 250 per annual return per year; persistent non-filing (typically 3 consecutive years) triggers a final warning and subsequent administrative strike-off by CIPC under Section 82 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (integrated with Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Annual Return (within 30 business days of incorporation anniversary); any material change in UBO must be lodged within 10 business days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to disclose beneficial ownership is a criminal offence under the Companies Act; CIPC may impose fines up to ZAR 500,000 or imprisonment for directors/officers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the public interest score exceeds 350, or for all private companies that are not managed by their shareholders. A private company with a public interest score below 350 is generally required to undergo an independent review unless exempted. The public interest score is calculated from average employees, third-party liability, revenue, and shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; alternatively, IFRS for SMEs (as adopted in South Africa) is available for eligible non-public entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each Annual Return filing, the company must confirm its Beneficial Ownership Register details to the CIPC. Any shareholding transfer or direct/indirect change in beneficial ownership during the year must be recorded in the Beneficial Ownership Register and filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the change. The company secretary or director must verify the accuracy of the UBO data and issue a signed confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Accounting Records (Reflecting Assets, Liabilities, Revenue, and Expenses)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; previously 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday; targeted incentives only. Key reliefs affecting agro-chemical trading: accelerated depreciation for qualifying plant/machinery (s12C); capital expenditure allowance for grid-connected renewable energy (s12B); Research & Development 150% deduction (s11D) where applicable; exemption of certain foreign dividends/interest under participation exemptions (s10B/s10B(2)) for SA-resident companies; no CIT payable on capital gains on disposal of shares under participation exemption (s10B) subject to conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no fixed expiry; assessed losses are ring-fenced where the taxpaying company fails the s20A 'same trade' continuity test or where more than 50% shareholding change occurs without active business continuity)
